 Dated this the 11th day of March, 2025.
 Judgment

The petitioners in O.P.(MV) No. 548 of 2016 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Thalassery filed this appeal challenging the dismissal of a claim petition under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('the Act' for short).
2. The petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased Thaharaz, who died in a motor vehicle accident.

According to the petitioners, on 04.07.2015, while the deceased was riding a scooter and overtaking a bus stopped in a bus stop at the place of the accident, the 1st respondent suddenly moved the bus towards the right side without caring for the scooter and thereby, hitting the scooter and causing serious injuries to the rider of the scooter, who subsequently succumbed to his injuries on the same day.
3. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exhibits A1 to A6 were marked from the side of the petitioners, and from the side of the respondents, RWs 1 and 2 were examined and Exhibits B1 to B5
were marked.

4. The Tribunal recorded a finding that the evidence of PW1 regarding the occurrence is not reliable and that the petitioners have not succeeded in proving the involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident and therefore, respondents are not liable to pay any compensation and hence, dismissed the petition.
5. Heard Sri. C.P. Peethambaran, the learned counsel for the appellants and Sri. P.K. Manoj Kumar,
the learned counsel for the respondent insurance company.

6. The learned counsel for the appellants argued that the petitioners have examined an independent witness as PW1 to prove the occurrence and PW1 has clearly stated in the chief affidavit that he witnessed the occurrence and that the deceased was riding the vehicle in front of his vehicle and while the deceased was attempting to overtake the bus stopped there in the bus stop, the driver of the bus suddenly moved the bus towards right and thereby, the bus caused to hit the vehicle of the deceased and the deceased fell down and sustained serious injuries.

entities.text: Abdurahiman vs Moideen Koya on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW1 has specifically stated that the accident occurred only because the driver of the bus moved the bus towards right by ignoring the vehicles coming from behind and that there was no negligence on the part of the deceased.
In cross examination also, PW1 reiterated that he witnessed the occurrence at a distance of 20 metres and at that time, he was traveling as a pillion rider in another motorcycle.
In cross examination, PW1 categorically deposed that he saw the bus hitting the scooter and he denied the suggestion that the bus never caused to hit the scooter.

8. In New India Assurance Co.Ltd. v. Pazhaniammal and Others (2011(3) KHC 595), this Court held that as a general rule, production of the police charge sheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of a claim under Section 166 of the Motor vehicles Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co.Ltd. v. Pazhaniammal and Others (2011(3) KHC 595)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said decision, it was also held that if any one of the parties do not accept such charge sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce oral evidence and if oral evidence is adduced by any party in a case where charge sheet is filed, the Tribunals should give further opportunity to others also to adduce oral evidence and in such a case, the charge sheet will pale into insignificance and the dispute will have to be decided on the basis of the evidence.
It was further held that in all other cases, such charge sheet can be reckoned as sufficient evidence of negligence in a claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

9. The decision of the Hon'ble Supreme court in Mathew Alexander v. Muhammed Shafi (2023 INSC 621) shows that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner need not be established by the claimants and that the claimants need only to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.

entities.text: Mathew Alexander v. Muhammed Shafi (2023 INSC 621)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, it was also held that the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt cannot be applied while considering the petition seeking compensation on account of death or injury in a road traffic accident.

10. It is well settled that grant of compensation under Section 163A of the Act on the basis of structured formula is required to be made without any requirement of any proof of negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident.

The evidence of PW1 clearly shows that bus bearing No. KL-13 L/314 is involved in the accident and the Tribunal has failed to appreciate the evidence of PW1 on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.

11. It is not in dispute that the Investigating Officer has seized the bus in connection with the accident and the same was also examined by RW2, Motor Vehicle Inspector, in the premises of the Police Station.

Therefore, I find that the Tribunal is not justified in recording a finding that the bus is not involved in the accident by rejecting the evidence of PW1 to exonerate the respondents from liability under Section 163A of the Act.

Hence, the said findings of the Tribunal is liable to be set aside and the matter requires to be remanded to the Tribunal, for deciding the quantum of compensation payable to the appellants under Section 163A of the Act.

12. In the result, the findings in the impugned award regarding the non-involvement of the bus in the accident and dismissal of the claim petition are set aside and the matter is remanded to the Tribunal for deciding the quantum of compensation payable to the claim petitioners under Section 163A of the Act.
The parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 11.04.2025.
